subject: chem
source: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620) syllabus for examination in 2026, 2027 and 2028 — Cambridge International; Year 10 covers topics 1–8 (first half of the two-year course)

weeks.topic: States of matter: solids, liquids, gases and changes of state
objectives: Describe the properties of solids, liquids and gases
Explain melting, boiling, evaporation, condensation and freezing using particle theory
Interpret heating and cooling curves

weeks.topic: Kinetic particle theory, gas pressure and diffusion
objectives: Explain the effect of temperature and pressure on gas volume
Describe diffusion in terms of particle movement
Explain how relative molecular mass affects the rate of diffusion

weeks.topic: Elements, compounds and mixtures
objectives: Distinguish between elements, compounds and mixtures
Describe the differences between metals and non-metals

weeks.topic: Atomic structure: protons, neutrons, electrons and electronic configuration
objectives: State the relative charges and masses of subatomic particles
Define proton number and mass number
Write electronic configurations for the first 20 elements

weeks.topic: Isotopes and relative atomic mass
objectives: Define isotopes and explain why they have the same chemical properties
Calculate relative atomic mass from isotopic abundances

weeks.topic: Ions and ionic bonding
objectives: Describe how ions form by electron loss or gain
Draw dot-and-cross diagrams for ionic compounds
Relate the giant lattice structure to the properties of ionic compounds

weeks.topic: Simple molecules and covalent bonding
objectives: Describe covalent bonds as shared pairs of electrons
Draw dot-and-cross diagrams for H2, Cl2, H2O, CH4, NH3, CO2 and others
Explain the low melting points of simple molecular substances

weeks.topic: Giant covalent structures: diamond, graphite and silicon(IV) oxide
objectives: Describe the structures of diamond, graphite and silicon(IV) oxide
Relate structure to properties and uses

weeks.topic: Metallic bonding
objectives: Describe metallic bonding as positive ions in a sea of delocalised electrons
Explain electrical conductivity, malleability and high melting points of metals

weeks.topic: Formulas, state symbols and balancing chemical equations
objectives: Deduce formulae of ionic compounds from ion charges
Write balanced symbol equations with state symbols
Write ionic equations

weeks.topic: Relative formula mass and the mole
objectives: Calculate relative formula mass
Use the mole and the Avogadro constant
Convert between mass, moles and molar mass

weeks.topic: Reacting masses, limiting reactants and percentage yield
objectives: Calculate reacting masses from balanced equations
Identify limiting reactants
Calculate percentage yield

weeks.topic: Molar gas volume and concentration of solutions
objectives: Use 24 dm³ as the molar gas volume at room temperature
Calculate concentration in g/dm³ and mol/dm³
Convert between cm³ and dm³

weeks.topic: Empirical and molecular formulae; percentage purity and composition
objectives: Calculate empirical formulae from masses or percentages
Deduce molecular formulae from relative mass
Calculate percentage purity and percentage composition

weeks.topic: Review: particles, atomic structure, bonding and stoichiometry
objectives: Revise bonding diagrams and structure–property links
Practise multi-step mole calculations

weeks.topic: Electrolysis of molten compounds and aqueous solutions
objectives: Define electrolysis and identify electrodes and electrolyte
Predict products of electrolysis of molten and aqueous compounds
Describe the electrolysis of brine and copper(II) sulfate

weeks.topic: Electrolysis: ionic half-equations and electroplating
objectives: Write ionic half-equations at each electrode
Describe electroplating and refining of copper

weeks.topic: Hydrogen–oxygen fuel cells
objectives: Describe how a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell produces electricity
Compare fuel cells with petrol engines

weeks.topic: Exothermic and endothermic reactions; reaction pathway diagrams
objectives: Define exothermic and endothermic reactions
Draw and interpret reaction pathway diagrams
Identify activation energy and enthalpy change

weeks.topic: Bond energies and enthalpy change calculations
objectives: Explain bond breaking as endothermic and bond making as exothermic
Calculate enthalpy change from bond energies

weeks.topic: Physical and chemical changes; factors affecting rate of reaction
objectives: Distinguish physical and chemical changes
Describe the effects of concentration, pressure, surface area, temperature and catalysts on rate

weeks.topic: Collision theory and rate investigations
objectives: Explain rate changes using collision theory and activation energy
Investigate rate by measuring gas volume or mass loss
Interpret rate graphs

weeks.topic: Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium
objectives: Describe reversible reactions such as hydrated copper(II) sulfate
Explain dynamic equilibrium
Predict the effect of changing conditions on equilibrium position

weeks.topic: The Haber process and the Contact process
objectives: State the conditions used in the Haber and Contact processes
Explain the compromise between rate, yield and cost

weeks.topic: Redox: oxidation, reduction, oxidising and reducing agents
objectives: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of oxygen, electrons and oxidation number
Identify oxidising and reducing agents
Use Roman numerals in names

weeks.topic: Properties of acids and bases; pH and indicators
objectives: Describe reactions of acids with metals, bases and carbonates
Use the pH scale and universal indicator
Identify H+ and OH– ions in acids and alkalis

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: topics 1–6 (states of matter to chemical reactions)
objectives: Complete timed papers on content taught so far
Use mark schemes to correct calculation errors

weeks.topic: Strong and weak acids, neutralisation and proton transfer
objectives: Compare strong and weak acids
Describe neutralisation as H+ + OH– → H2O
Define acids as proton donors and bases as proton acceptors

weeks.topic: Oxides: acidic, basic and amphoteric
objectives: Classify oxides as acidic, basic, neutral or amphoteric
Relate metallic and non-metallic character to oxide type

weeks.topic: Preparation of soluble salts and solubility rules
objectives: Prepare a soluble salt from an acid and an insoluble base
Use titration for salts from alkalis
Apply general solubility rules

weeks.topic: Preparation of insoluble salts by precipitation; water of crystallisation
objectives: Prepare an insoluble salt by precipitation
Define hydrated, anhydrous and water of crystallisation

weeks.topic: Arrangement of elements in the Periodic Table
objectives: Describe groups and periods
Relate group number to outer-shell electrons
Describe the change from metallic to non-metallic character across a period

weeks.topic: Group I alkali metals: properties and trends
objectives: Describe the reactions of lithium, sodium and potassium with water
Predict properties of other Group I elements from trends

weeks.topic: Group VII halogens: properties and displacement reactions
objectives: Describe the colours and states of chlorine, bromine and iodine
Explain halogen displacement reactions
Predict trends down the group

weeks.topic: Transition elements and noble gases
objectives: Describe the properties of transition elements including variable oxidation states and coloured compounds
Explain the unreactivity of noble gases and their uses

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: topics 1–8
objectives: Complete end-of-year papers on all Year 10 content
Apply knowledge in practical and data questions

weeks.topic: Review: salt preparation and Periodic Table trends before Year 11
objectives: Correct errors from end-of-year exams
Consolidate salt preparation methods and group trends
